exam.title: Administering Windows Server
exam.study_prerequisites: Several years of Windows Server experience plus practical AD DS, Group Policy, PowerShell and delegated administration, Hyper-V and Azure VMs, DNS/DHCP, SMB and Windows storage, Azure Arc, security hardening, Azure Monitor, and evidence-led troubleshooting.

objective_coverage.objective_group: Deploy and manage Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS)
Manage Windows Server instances and workloads in a hybrid environment
Implement and manage an on-premises and hybrid networking infrastructure
Monitor and troubleshoot Windows Server environments

review.notes: All seven objective groups and published subobjectives are indexed to guide sections. The September 7 best-effort pass registered Microsoft transport and lab evidence plus qualified Ubuntu, Red Hat-family, SUSE/openSUSE, Oracle Linux, systemd, libvirt, Microsoft Press, and expert sources. The source-validation outcome remains blocked because no current Microsoft end-to-end SSH Direct implementation contract or compatibility matrix was found; the guide teaches the provisional model, confidence levels, and a versioned validation plan without presenting it as universal support. The remaining domains retain three scenarios, eight labs, and 28 checks. All 79 cited URLs are cataloged: 74 reachable, five O'Reilly/MeasureUp/Udemy pages access-blocked, and none missing.

sources.title: Windows Server 2019 Inside Out sample
sources.notes: Historical hvc.exe SSH example tied to Windows Server 2019-era material; corroboration, not a current support matrix.

sources.title: Hyper-V Socket Support for the built-in hvc.exe SSH command
sources.notes: Community-authored open issue with useful diagnostic tracing; neither product documentation nor a support commitment.

sources.title: HVC - SSH Direct for Linux VMs on Hyper-V
sources.notes: Named-expert preview-era explanation and field comments; retain its age and configuration-sensitive behavior.

sources.title: Ubuntu hv_sock OpenSSH socket-activation regression
sources.notes: Current distribution bug evidence comparing Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 behavior; useful failure evidence, not a universal recipe or support statement.

sources.title: Virtualizing Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 on Hyper-V
sources.notes: Historical RHEL Hyper-V integration evidence; predates the SSH Direct objective and does not document hvc.exe or VSOCK SSH activation.

sources.title: RHEL 8.5 release notes: socat AF_VSOCK support
sources.notes: Confirms AF_VSOCK listen/connect support in RHEL's socat package; a diagnostic building block, not end-to-end Hyper-V SSH Direct proof.

sources.title: RHEL 10.2 AF_VSOCK namespace parameters
sources.notes: Current RHEL AF_VSOCK namespace behavior; does not establish Hyper-V transport packaging, OpenSSH configuration, or hvc.exe interoperability.

sources.title: CentOS Stream 9 kernel modules include hv_sock
sources.notes: Third-party package-index evidence for one CentOS Stream build; verify the installed signed package and do not treat CentOS Stream as a RHEL support statement.

sources.title: Fedora 44 OpenSSH server package inventory
sources.notes: Fedora-owned inventory of OpenSSH socket units; does not prove a VSOCK listener, Hyper-V transport, or RHEL-equivalent packaging.

sources.title: Fedora 44 SELinux policy SSHD VSOCK rules
sources.notes: Fedora policy evidence for SSHD VSOCK sockets; not a RHEL support statement or an hvc.exe validation.

sources.title: SUSE 16 kernel package hv_sock maintenance
sources.notes: Current SUSE kernel maintenance evidence for hv_sock; does not identify a supported SLES SSH Direct matrix or install a guest listener.

sources.title: openSUSE Factory OpenSSH VSOCK listener packaging change
sources.notes: Archived Factory package change for a libvirt-oriented SSHD VSOCK listener; Hyper-V and SLES applicability remain unverified.

sources.title: SUSE Package Hub virtme SSH-over-VSOCK history
sources.notes: SUSE package evidence for SSH-over-VSOCK as a maintained pattern; targets virtme/KVM rather than Hyper-V hvc.exe.

sources.title: Oracle Linux VSOCK interface configuration
sources.notes: Current generic Oracle Linux KVM VSOCK configuration; does not establish Oracle Linux as a Hyper-V SSH Direct guest, and UEK/RHCK remain separate tests.

sources.title: Linux Integration Services 4.1 Hyper-V sockets guide
sources.notes: Historical hv_sock evidence for named enterprise distributions and kernels; old, does not configure SSH, and cannot establish current support.

sources.title: systemd VM interface
sources.notes: Maintained upstream evidence that systemd 256+ can bind SSH to AF_VSOCK port 22; distribution enablement and Hyper-V hvc.exe interoperability remain unproven.

sources.title: Libvirt SSH proxy
sources.notes: Maintained upstream VSOCK SSH implementation guidance for QEMU/libvirt; a cross-distribution model, not Hyper-V SSH Direct support evidence.

findings.title: dMSA needs supported DC and application hosts
findings.evidence: Current FAQ requires discoverable Windows Server 2025 DC and supported hosts; gMSA migration and account merging are unsupported.

findings.title: GPU-P compatibility and surviving capacity are separate
findings.evidence: Current docs require supported hardware/drivers and homogeneous configuration; migration uses TCP/IP compression and can need more CPU/time. Multiple assigned partitions are documented.
findings.recommendation: Add bounded two-node capacity example; qualify the older blog's single-partition statement.
findings.resolution: Add bounded two-node capacity example; qualify the older blog's single-partition statement.

findings.title: Tiered filenames do not establish offline content availability
findings.evidence: Current planning guidance distinguishes SMB cloud endpoint, NTFS server volume and agent HTTPS transport.
findings.recommendation: Add branch-outage cache example and separate client SMB access from sync transport.
findings.resolution: Add branch-outage cache example and separate client SMB access from sync transport.

findings.title: Server 2025 signing default differs from Windows 11 24H2
findings.evidence: Current signing docs specify outbound required by default on Server 2025; relevant Windows 11 editions require both directions.
findings.recommendation: Correct default and require effective-policy evidence; explain guest incompatibility.
findings.resolution: Correct default and require effective-policy evidence; explain guest incompatibility.

findings.title: Installed 2026 updates govern RC4 enforcement
findings.evidence: April enforcement and July removal of the temporary rollback switch supersede historical future guidance.
findings.recommendation: Add versioned account-key and ticket checks rather than blanket RC4 claims.
findings.resolution: Add versioned account-key and ticket checks rather than blanket RC4 claims.

findings.title: Direct AMA telemetry preview has retired
findings.evidence: July 31, 2026 retirement stops the old AgentDirectToStore path.
findings.recommendation: Teach current Logs and export route and distinguish configuration from delivered telemetry.
findings.resolution: Teach current Logs and export route and distinguish configuration from delivered telemetry.

findings.title: VM Insights Map is not a new dependency-mapping recommendation
findings.evidence: Map and Dependency Agent retire June 30, 2028 with onboarding restrictions; performance collection is a separate capability.
findings.recommendation: Replace generic process/dependency mapping advice with scoped lifecycle guidance.
findings.resolution: Replace generic process/dependency mapping advice with scoped lifecycle guidance.

findings.title: SSH Direct supported guest implementation remains unverified
findings.evidence: Transport architecture is public, but no verified current supported end-to-end guest recipe was found; historical CentOS package evidence now returns 404.
findings.recommendation: Keep the support limitation visible pending authoritative evidence.
